messages:
mara: Preflight failed on infra/gitops -> prod sync (job: gitops/preflight-prod-2175). Error: 'annotation mismatch: podAffinity/podAntiAffinity present in prod but missing in staging'. Blocked by policy/k8s-affinity-check. Anyone seen this before?
drftbot: automated-diff: detected 1 chart drift in charts/model-serving: `podAntiAffinity` block present in prod values (values.prod.yaml) but removed in staging values. Also: tolerations.gpu present in prod, absent in staging.
jay: uuugh, that's my change. I removed the `podAntiAffinity` default to improve packing density across hosts, but the helm conditional accidentally evaluates differently for staging values file -> whole block got omitted.
olivia: that matches the Pending GPU pods we saw earlier in staging (09:18). Without the anti-affinity staging ended up binpacking and then couldn't schedule some other workloads that expected spread.
ryan: FYI terraform plan shows the eu-west nodepool autoscaler config diverged too (staging azBias -> higher spot fallback). If we reintroduce anti-affinity in staging we might temporarily need extra nodes until binpacking stabilizes.
tis: repro commands:
```
# show rendered diff between envs
tools/gitops-diff --from=staging --to=prod --filter=charts/model-serving
# or render and server-dry-run
helm template ./charts/model-serving -f values.staging.yaml | kubectl diff -f - --server-side
```
jay: quick remediate options:
- add a templating guard so the antiAffinity block doesn't get dropped by conditionals
- patch staging values to explicitly set `affinity: { podAntiAffinity: { preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution: ... } }` and rerun preflight
- or add a temporary GitOps override to keep staging aligned until chart fix lands

here's a minimal values snippet to re-add: 
```yaml
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        podAffinityTerm:
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: model-serving
```
ops-bot: canary patch applied to namespace `staging-canary` and preflight re-triggered.
driftbot: preflight result: failed -> now passing when staging override set `affinity.podAntiAffinity` true.
olivia: cost question: re-introducing anti-affinity will spread pods and lower per-node GPU utilization. What's the hit?
ryan: back-of-envelope: with our typical 500k token/day workload, enforcing hostname anti-affinity increases node footprint ~12% at peak for model-serving fleet in us-west1. Rough incremental cost ~+$2.8k/month (on current committed pricing). Also short spike in autoscaler activity for ~30-90 mins during rollout.
mara: proposed plan: jay will open a PR to fix the chart templating + add a unit test rendering the antiAffinity branch; we add a GitOps preflight assertion to fail if affinity keys diverge across envs; temporary override applied to staging until PR merges. SRE on-call to monitor allocator headroom and node-autoscaler.
jay: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/482 — fixes conditional and adds chart unit test + changelog. Will include values.staging.yaml explicit affinity.
tis: also propose OPA tweak: allow a controlled rollout label `rollout/allow-affinity-drift` so future intentional differences can pass preflight while under review. Policy: policy/k8s-affinity-check should accept that label.
ryan: runbook items: watch `allocator.gpu_utilization`, `cluster.autoscaler.scale_up_count`, and `kube-scheduler.pending_pods{reason=Unschedulable}` for 1h after merge.
mara: I'll merge the PR after smoke tests in staging-canary and a 30m observation window. @ops-bot please schedule canary rollout to prod with 10% traffic and auto-rollback if pending pods > 5 for 20m. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: scheduled canary: model-serving v2.1 -> 10% traffic. Auto-rollback hook set.
jay: thanks all — will follow up in PR thread with test artifacts and rendered manifests to prove parity.
mara: moving to close this thread once PR merged and metrics stable. Good catch to the preflight checks — saved us a noisy outage in prod. :heart:
